mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates easy monetary conditions, which may stimulate borrowing and investment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 60% of the 20-day windows following low FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate above 5% signals labor market weakness, potentially leading to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer spending may decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows when UNRATE exceeds 5%.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) is strong but unemployment (UNRATE) is rising, it may indicate inefficiencies in the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows when GDPC1 and UNRATE diverge.

mechanism_narrative: Rapid growth in housing starts (HOUST) during an economic expansion may signal an overheating market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as a correction unfolds.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 60-day windows following rapid HOUST growth.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in employment growth (PAYEMS) may indicate a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 60% of the 20-day windows when PAYEMS growth slows.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strong economic activity, which may boost corporate earnings and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following INDPRO increases.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) combined with low unemployment (UNRATE) may indicate tight monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows when FEDFUNDS are high and UNRATE is low.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in real consumer spending (RSAFS) may indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days as corporate revenues increase.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following RSAFS growth.
